newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian LSWR prices seen to rise on winter demand.
newsitem.headline: Asian LSWR prices seen to rise on winter demand.

text.p: Prices of Indonesian low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR), a fuel used for power generation, are poised for recovery on North Asian winter demand while Indonesian supplies stay stable, industry sources said on Friday.

Traders said while North Asian imports are expected to increase due to strong demand for the burning fuel during winter, South Korean demand is due to rise with the government expected to raise winter stockpiling requirements.
Traders said South Korean domestic LSWR supplies have already been stemmed with the one-month shutdown of refiner Yukong's 265,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) crude unit since since October 15.
They assessed South Korean November imports for LSWR at 1.1 million barrels, 300,000 barrels more than its estimated imports in October.

Traders said South Korean refiner Hanwha Energy is expected to import a further 300,000 barrels for early December delivery, after already having purchased 400,000 barrels of LSWR for mid-November loading from Indonesia.
Hanwha is said to have paid a premium of around 20 cents per barrel over the Pertamina price formula, 10 cents lower from assessment seen a week ago.
But traders said premiums were currently assessed considerably firmer at 40-50 cents.

Although Japan is expected to import 800,000 barrels in November, stable from its estimated imports in October, some traders said import volumes may be bigger as power companies emerge with requirements.
A trader told Reuters, Japan's power company, Kansai Electric Power Co has a requirement for 200,000 barrels of LSWR for early December delivery.
"We have already heard some enquiries for top-up cargoes by a few shosha (Japanese traders) here (in Singapore)," said European major.

Traders said Japanese buyers were looking to buy LSWR as the price of Indonesian crudes, the alternative burning fuel, are expensive - Minas is priced around $21.70 per barrel in the international crude market, and Duri around $21.20.
This compares with spot market quotes for LSWR at $18.30-$18.80 per barrel on Thursday.
Low Asian LSWR prices have also opened the arbitrage window to the U.S. with at least two cargoes, or around 600,000 barrels heard heading west.
This would push total demand for Indonesian LSWR in November to 3.66 million barrels, including exports of between 400,000-600,000 barrels to India and the usual term supply of 560,000 to Italy.
Asian LSWR prices in the Singapore spot market have fallen by a dollar since late October as demand was slack while Indonesia raised exports.
But Indonesia state-owned oil company, Pertamina made a smaller LSWR allocation in November, a total of 4 million barrels, compared to 4.2 million barrels in October.

Traders said Pertamina may allocate more LSWR supplies in November as two secondary processing units at its Balongan refinery were shut for maintenance. A 83,000 bpd cracking unit was shut for 60 days since October 1 and another 58,000 bpd down at the same time for 40 days.
The secondary processing unit refines LSWR to produce lighter distillates.
But Indonesian affiliates have yet to received any details from Pertamina on the additional supplies.
-- Singapore newsroom (65-870-3082).
